body_markdown:
Manthey, a German racing team and engineering company[closely linked with Porsche](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-mustang-gtd-competition-nurburgring-time/) , is celebrating its 30th birthday. The brand unveiled a pair of race cars: the Porsche 911 GT3 Cup MR 30 and the Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Clubsport MR 30 to mark the occasion. Both are limited-edition, track-only models that feature mechanical updates and commemorative styling.


Extensively tested on the Nürburgring among other tracks, the GT3 Cup MR 30 is based on the 992.1-generation 911. Manthey increased the flat-six’s displacement from 4.0 to 4.2 liters to unlock about 552 horsepower, up from 503 in the regular-production GT3. The engine spins the rear wheels via a six-speed sequential transmission, and cooling system updates keep the extra power in check. While the standard 911 GT3 is[hugely capable on the track](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-911-gt3-manual-nurburgring-time/) , the MR 30 further benefits from six-way-adjustable coilovers.


Manthey also added a full body kit that includes canards on the front bumper, wheel arch extensions that widen the track, and a rear wing, all made with recycled carbon fiber. Forged center-locking wheels with an edition-specific design add a finishing touch to the look while reducing unsprung weight. Inside, a “30 Years of Manthey” badge identifies this 911 as a limited-edition car.

The GT4 RS Clubsport MR 30 is marketed as the ultimate Manthey-tuned evolution of the current-generation Cayman. Production ended in 2025, and the model’s successor (which will be available with electric power) hasn’t made its debut yet. Manthey kept the 500-horsepower flat-six and added a carbon fiber body kit that generates more downforce, as well as lightweight wheels. Several anniversary-specific details, including the “30 Years Anniversary” logo on the wing’s end plates, are also part of the package.


Production of Manthey’s Porsche 911 GT3 Cup MR 30 and Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS Clubsport MR 30 is limited to 15 units each. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet. Manthey will accept orders until October 30, 2026, and allocate build slots shortly after. Deliveries of the Cayman will begin in November 2027, while 911 buyers will need to wait until early 2027 to get their car.
